categories.label: Prompting
categories.description: Give AI a clear job, useful context, and smart limits.

categories.label: Ethics
categories.description: Use AI honestly, fairly, and with human responsibility.

categories.label: Data & Privacy
categories.description: Protect personal information and share only what is needed.

categories.label: Verification
categories.description: Check claims, sources, dates, and evidence before trusting AI.

questions.question: You ask AI, “Help me with my science project.” What is the best next move?
options: Add the topic, grade level, goal, materials, and the kind of help you want
Type the same request in all capital letters
Ask AI to finish the entire project
Remove every detail so AI can be more creative
questions.explanation: A useful prompt names the task, context, constraints, and desired output.

questions.question: Which prompt gives AI the clearest audience and format?
options: Tell me about recycling
Write something good about recycling
Explain recycling in five bullet points for a sixth-grade class
Give me every fact about recycling
questions.explanation: The audience, length, and format make the request clear and usable.

questions.question: AI’s first answer sounds too advanced. What should you do?
options: Accept it because AI probably knows best
Ask it to rewrite the answer for your grade level and define difficult terms
Delete the assignment
Keep asking “Why?” with no context
questions.explanation: A follow-up prompt can adjust the reading level and clarify exactly what needs to change.

questions.question: You want feedback without having AI replace your writing. Which prompt is strongest?
options: Write a perfect paragraph for me
Make this better
Grade me and do not explain why
Point out two unclear sentences and ask me questions that will help me revise them
questions.explanation: The prompt keeps you as the writer while asking AI for specific, useful feedback.

questions.question: Why might you include an example in a prompt?
options: It shows the style or format you are aiming for
It guarantees every fact will be correct
It lets you skip reviewing the answer
It makes private information safe to share
questions.explanation: An example helps AI understand the desired style or structure, but you still need to review the result.

questions.question: A big task keeps producing messy answers. What is the best prompting strategy?
options: Add random words to the prompt
Ask for everything in one giant response
Break the task into smaller steps and handle one step at a time
Let AI decide what the assignment means
questions.explanation: Breaking a complex task into clear steps makes each request easier to guide and check.

questions.question: Which detail is most useful when asking AI to build a three-day study plan?
options: Your favorite color
The topics, available time, quiz date, and materials you must use
A friend’s password
A request to make the plan impossible to change
questions.explanation: A realistic plan needs the actual topics, schedule, deadline, and learning materials.

questions.question: What is a smart limit to include when asking AI for presentation ideas?
options: Use as many slides as possible
Invent any missing sources
Make every decision for the group
Suggest no more than five ideas that can be completed with our available time
questions.explanation: A clear limit keeps the answer focused on options your group can actually use.

questions.question: AI writes a full response for an assignment that should show your thinking. What is the most ethical move?
options: Submit it unchanged and do not mention AI
Use it as a thinking aid, write your own response, and follow your teacher’s AI rules
Change two words and claim it is entirely yours
Ask AI to make it harder to detect
questions.explanation: Ethical use keeps the learning and final responsibility with you and follows the rules for disclosure.

questions.question: An AI image generator keeps showing only one kind of person as a “scientist.” What should you do?
options: Notice the bias, revise the request, and review the results critically
Assume the images represent every scientist
Hide the pattern from the group
Use the first image because it was fastest
questions.explanation: Fair AI use means noticing biased patterns and taking steps to include missing perspectives.

questions.question: Who is responsible for a decision made with help from AI?
options: Nobody, because a computer was involved
Only the company that made the AI
The human using the advice and the people responsible for the decision
The AI chatbot itself
questions.explanation: Humans remain responsible for reviewing AI output and for the real-world decisions they make.

questions.question: Your group uses AI to organize shared notes. What keeps the work fair?
options: Let one person take credit for everything
Erase the original contributions
Hide the use of AI even if disclosure is required
Keep everyone’s contributions visible and agree on how AI will be used
questions.explanation: Fair group work preserves people’s contributions and uses shared rules everyone understands.

questions.question: A friend asks you to make an AI voice clip that sounds like your principal saying something fake. What is the best response?
options: Do it if the clip is short
Refuse because impersonation can deceive and harm people
Post it first and explain later
Make it sound even more realistic
questions.explanation: Using AI to impersonate someone without permission can deceive others and cause real harm.

questions.question: When should you tell an audience that AI helped create something?
options: When the rules, context, or audience expects disclosure
Never
Only when the result has a typo
Only after someone catches you
questions.explanation: Honest disclosure follows the rules and helps the audience understand how the work was made.

questions.question: AI suggests a punishment for a student. What is the safest ethical approach?
options: Use it immediately because AI is neutral
Let AI make the final decision
Have responsible adults review the facts, rules, possible bias, and impact
Avoid telling the student how the choice was made
questions.explanation: High-impact decisions need human judgment, due process, context, and a careful bias check.

questions.question: AI produces an idea that closely copies a living artist’s distinctive work. What is the strongest next move?
options: Claim you invented the style
Remove the artist’s name but copy everything else
Sell it immediately
Create a more original direction and respect the artist’s work and usage rules
questions.explanation: Ethical creation respects other people’s work and pushes toward an original result.

questions.question: You want AI to help summarize a student incident report. What should you do first?
options: Paste the full report with names and contact details
Remove identifying details and use only an approved tool and process
Post the report publicly
Add more private details for context
questions.explanation: Sensitive records require approved tools, minimal information, and removal of identifying details.

questions.question: Which item should never be placed in an AI prompt?
options: A public book title
A made-up character name
A question about fractions
Your password or login code
questions.explanation: Passwords and login codes are secrets and should never be shared with an AI tool.

questions.question: AI needs an example email to help improve the tone. What is the safest approach?
options: Replace names and private details with placeholders before sharing
Include everyone’s addresses and phone numbers
Upload the whole inbox
Use a stranger’s real email instead
questions.explanation: Placeholders preserve the useful structure without exposing personal information.

questions.question: What does “share only what is needed” mean?
options: Share every file in case one becomes useful
Share the smallest amount of information required for the task
Share private information if the answer will be faster
Let the tool decide what it wants
questions.explanation: Data minimization reduces risk by limiting the information sent to a tool.

questions.question: A photo includes a student ID badge and a home address on a package. Before using the photo with AI, you should:
options: Upload it at full size
Add the student’s schedule
Crop or blur the private details—or do not upload the photo
Assume nobody will notice
questions.explanation: Images can expose private information too; remove sensitive details or keep the image out of the tool.

questions.question: You are unsure whether a school AI tool is approved for student data. What should you do?
options: Use it secretly
Ask a teacher or responsible adult and check the school’s approved-tool rules
Create a fake account with another person’s name
Upload the data and delete it later
questions.explanation: When data rules are unclear, pause and confirm the approved tool and process first.

questions.question: Why can location information be sensitive?
options: It can reveal where someone lives, studies, or spends time
It always makes an AI answer incorrect
It changes the font in the answer
It is only private on weekends
questions.explanation: Location can reveal routines and personal places, so it should be shared only when truly necessary and safe.

questions.question: Which prompt uses privacy-safe placeholder language?
options: Write about Maria Lopez at 14 Oak Street
Use student ID 482917 and this medical note
Summarize Student A’s fictional schedule without real names or records
Remember my password for next time
questions.explanation: A generic placeholder can provide useful context without revealing a real person’s identity.

questions.question: AI gives you a surprising statistic with no source. What should you do?
options: Use it because it sounds confident
Ask for evidence and verify it with a reliable source
Repeat it until it feels true
Remove the number but keep the claim
questions.explanation: A confident statistic still needs a real, reliable source that you check yourself.

questions.question: What matters most when checking AI information about a current event?
options: The answer’s font
How quickly AI responded
The source, publication date, and whether multiple reliable reports agree
Whether the answer is long
questions.explanation: Current events change quickly, so source quality, date, and corroboration matter.

questions.question: AI provides a quotation for your history project. What is the strongest check?
options: Find the quote in the original or a trustworthy primary source
Trust the quotation marks
Use it if it sounds old-fashioned
Ask AI to repeat it twice
questions.explanation: Quotes should be checked against the original source for exact wording and context.

questions.question: AI lists three articles, but one link does not exist. What does that tell you?
options: The other links must be perfect
The missing article is probably secret
Links are never useful
AI can invent citations, so every source needs to be opened and checked
questions.explanation: AI can fabricate convincing citations; verify that each source exists and actually supports the claim.

questions.question: AI solves a math problem. How should you verify the result?
options: Check the steps and calculate the answer another way
Accept it if the answer is bold
Skip the work because AI already did it
Choose the largest number
questions.explanation: Reviewing the reasoning and using a second method can catch confident calculation errors.

questions.question: An online image might be AI-generated or edited. What is the best first check?
options: Count the image’s colors
Trace the original source and compare reliable reporting or context
Believe the caption automatically
Share it quickly before it disappears
questions.explanation: Source tracing and reliable context are stronger than guessing from appearance alone.

questions.question: Two trustworthy sources disagree. What should you do?
options: Pick the one you like
Ask AI to hide the disagreement
Compare their evidence, dates, methods, and areas of agreement
Assume both are completely false
questions.explanation: Disagreement is a reason to inspect evidence and context more carefully, not to ignore it.

questions.question: Which source is usually strongest for confirming what a new school policy actually says?
options: An anonymous comment
A meme
AI’s summary with no link
The official published policy document
questions.explanation: The official document is the primary source for the policy’s actual language.
